seoTitle: How to See Volume Numbers in TradingView Clearly
metaDescription: Learn how to display actual volume numbers in TradingView, not just bars, by enabling volume labels and reading data values correctly for trading.
intro: Seeing volume bars on your chart is helpful, but sometimes you need the actual numeric values to make a more precise read. This guide shows how to enable volume labels in TradingView, adjust the indicator's settings, and understand what those numbers mean for your trading decisions. It's aimed at volume-based traders who want more than just a visual bar chart.

steps.heading: Add the volume indicator
steps.body: Open the indicators menu and apply the Volume indicator to your chart if it isn't already showing.

steps.heading: Enable volume numbers
steps.body: Adjust the indicator's settings to display numeric data values alongside or instead of just the volume bars.

steps.heading: Read volume correctly on the chart
steps.body: Compare volume numbers across different candles to understand which periods had unusually high or low trading activity.

steps.heading: Understand the difference between volume bars and values
steps.body: Volume bars give a quick visual comparison, while the actual numbers offer precise data for deeper analysis.

steps.heading: Apply tips to use volume for trade confirmation
steps.body: Use volume spikes alongside price movement to help confirm the strength or weakness behind a particular move.

faq.question: Why can't I see exact volume numbers by default?
faq.answer: TradingView's default volume display often shows bars for a quick visual reference, and you may need to adjust settings to reveal precise numeric values.

faq.question: Do volume numbers update in real time?
faq.answer: Yes, volume data typically updates in real time or near real time as new trading activity occurs during market hours.

faq.question: How can volume help confirm a price move?
faq.answer: A price move accompanied by high volume is often considered more significant than the same move on low volume, since it suggests stronger participation.

faq.question: Does volume data differ between asset classes?
faq.answer: Yes, how volume is measured and reported can vary between stocks, crypto, and forex, so it's worth understanding the context for the specific asset you're analyzing.
